builders.angle: LITERAL. Work BRIEF-r20's fix list 1 to 5 in order and exactly as written. Item 1 is a Steam Deck BUG, not a style note: with hud-late's load the strip must hold ONE row at 1280x800, legible, every folded group saying what it holds. Fix it first and prove it with the hud-late capture at both sizes before you touch anything else. Then the rail as one object, then the hand. The literal angle has won most recent rounds.

ONE CARVED RAIL. Item 2 is your round, and item 1 falls out of it: design the strip as a single carved object -- a brass-and-wood nameplate rail with ends, a surface and a shadow, built from round 19's hardware (ui/objects.js, prep_ui_hardware.py, kit.css's round-19 sections) -- with the readouts SET INTO it, and a rail that has a fixed budget at 1280 into which groups fold honestly ('10 Keepsakes' as one medallion that opens its tray). Then the boss under it (item 4), then the hand.

THE HAND FIRST. Item 3 is your round: at nine cards every NAME readable and the rules text ~11 px or more at 1280, the fan wide into the space between the piles, overlap pushed into the art window, the hovered or focused card rising clear. Measure it -- read the rendered title and rules font sizes and the overlap per card at both sizes -- then look. Then item 1, the rail's one row at 1280 on hud-late, because it is a bug on the same fight screens, and item 4 under it.
